reasoning_traces.think:
The core challenge is to transform noisy point estimates into well-calibrated probability statements. This requires a two-step process: first, characterizing the posterior uncertainty over model parameters, and second, constructing prediction intervals that maintain finite-sample coverage guarantees even when the model is misspecified. Conformal prediction provides a elegant solution by using the rank statistics of the training data to create distribution-free prediction bands. The resulting intervals are automatically calibrated, meaning they achieve the desired coverage rate regardless of the underlying data-generating process. This approach bridges the gap between Bayesian posterior inference and frequentist calibration, making it particularly suitable for high-stakes decision-making where miscalibration can lead to catastrophic consequences.
